name: Riverton
lore: Riverton is a small river-trading village on a slow brown river. Folk are plain-spoken and wary of strangers until coin changes hands. Barges and fishing boats bring most of the news, and the smell of river mud is never far away.

drowned_rat.name: The Drowned Rat
drowned_rat.lore: Riverton's oldest tavern, run by its sharp-tongued landlady, {{npc:hesk}}. Cheap ale, dice games and dockhands; it gets loud after dark.

common_room.name: Common Room
common_room.description: A low-beamed common room smelling of woodsmoke and spilled ale. A long oak bar runs along one wall, a fire crackles in a stone hearth, and a creaking staircase climbs to the rooms above.

exits.description: The front door opens onto the village square.
A creaking staircase.
A back door to the courtyard.

courtyard.name: Courtyard
courtyard.description: A cobbled courtyard behind the tavern, stacked with ale barrels and firewood. Steam and the smell of stew drift from the kitchen door; the stable stands across the yard.

exits.description: The back door into the common room.
The kitchen door.
Across the yard to the stable.
A heavy cellar door set into the flagstones, its iron ring worn smooth.

cellar.name: Cellar
cellar.description: A cold, low cellar under the courtyard, lined with ale casks and racks of dusty bottles. Water drips somewhere in the dark, and the air smells of damp stone and old beer.

exits.description: Wooden steps up to a heavy trapdoor.
A narrow door half-hidden behind the casks.
exits.traversal: Beyond the narrow door the passage is barely shoulder-wide: a long, stooping shuffle through dripping dark, rotten timbers creaking overhead.

kitchens.name: Kitchens
kitchens.description: Hot, smoky kitchens where a buxom, flour-dusted cook and two pretty scullery maids keep a stew pot bubbling over the fire. Strings of onions and hams hang from the rafters.

exits.description: Back out to the courtyard.

stable.name: Stable
stable.description: A straw-strewn stable with a few stalls, a water trough and a tired old mule. A wooden gate opens onto Market Lane.

exits.description: Out into the courtyard.
The stable gate onto Market Lane.

upstairs.name: Upstairs Rooms
upstairs.description: A narrow, quiet hallway with four plain guest rooms. The floorboards groan underfoot, the noise of the bar is only a murmur, and the window at the end looks out over the river.

exits.description: The staircase back down to the common room.

gilded_goose.name: The Gilded Goose
gilded_goose.lore: A newer, pricier inn that caters to merchants and barge captains. Polished brass, clean linen, and its host, Perrin Vale, an elegant, silver-gowned trans woman with a lovely laugh who looks down on the Drowned Rat.

common_room.name: Common Room
common_room.description: A bright common room with whitewashed walls, brass lamps and round tables set with linen. A painted goose with a gilt crown hangs over the bar, and a carpeted stair leads up.

exits.description: The door opens onto Market Lane.
A carpeted staircase.

upstairs.name: Upstairs Rooms
upstairs.description: The Goose's second floor: a carpeted corridor of well-kept rooms with brass numbers on the doors and a vase of river lilies on a side table.

exits.description: The carpeted staircase down to the common room.

general_store.name: Marlow's General Store
general_store.lore: A cluttered shop run by Marlow, a curvy, bespectacled beauty who sells a bit of everything and haggles over every copper with a sweet smile.

shop.name: Marlow's General Store
shop.description: Shelves crammed with rope, lamp oil, sacks of flour, fishing tackle and dusty oddments. A brass bell hangs over the door and Marlow's counter is buried in ledgers.

exits.description: The shop door, under the brass bell, opens onto Market Lane.

smithy.name: Brask's Smithy
smithy.lore: A hot, noisy forge run by Brask, a tall, broad-shouldered trans woman with soot-streaked arms and a confident grin, and her journeyman Tobin, a slender, pretty young man in his twenties who blushes easily. Horseshoes, boat fittings and the occasional blade.

forge.name: Brask's Smithy
forge.description: A soot-black workshop around a roaring forge. Hammers ring on the anvil, tools hang from every beam, and a water barrel hisses whenever hot iron is quenched.

exits.description: The open front of the forge looks onto Market Lane.

streets.name: Riverton Streets
streets.lore: Cobbled village streets, busy with carts, chickens and gossip by day and nearly empty after dark.

square.name: Village Square
square.description: A cobbled square around an old stone well. Market stalls line the edges, and roads lead off toward the river, the temple hill, Market Lane and the open country.

exits.description: The Drowned Rat's swinging sign hangs over the door.
A muddy lane slopes down to the river.
Steps climb the hill to the temple.
A narrow lane of shops.

market_lane.name: Market Lane
market_lane.description: A narrow lane of timber-framed shops. The Gilded Goose's gilt sign gleams on one side, Marlow's bell jangles on the other, and the clang of Brask's forge echoes from the end.

exits.description: The Gilded Goose.
The door of Marlow's General Store, propped open for custom.
Brask's Smithy, its forge open to the lane.
The Drowned Rat's stable gate.

docks.name: River Docks
docks.lore: Fishermen, bargemen and the occasional smuggler. Everyone here knows the river's moods.

piers.name: River Docks
piers.description: Weathered wooden piers jut into the slow brown river. Fishing boats bob at their moorings and gulls squabble over scraps.

exits.description: Back up the lane to the square.

temple.name: Temple of the Tides
temple.lore: A hushed, holy place tended by Sister Amara, a serene, dark-eyed beauty in sea-green robes. Voices drop to a whisper here; the village's bustle and suspicion stay outside.

nave.name: Temple of the Tides
nave.description: A small whitewashed temple on the hilltop. Inside, candles flicker before a carved statue of the river goddess, and the air smells of incense.

exits.description: The steps lead back down to the square.
An iron grate beside the altar, over a worn stone stair that descends into darkness.

catacombs.name: Temple Catacombs
catacombs.description: Narrow vaults cut into the hill beneath the temple. Niches of old bones line the walls, faded tide-marks are painted over the arches, and the candle smoke from above never quite reaches this deep.

exits.description: The stone stair up to the temple, behind the iron grate.
A low, rough-cut passage leading away into the dark.
exits.traversal: The passage is low and rough-cut; it is a long, cramped, stooping walk through the wet dark.

secret_tunnel.name: Secret Tunnel
secret_tunnel.lore: A forgotten smugglers' passage under the village. Few living folk know it exists.

tunnel.name: Secret Tunnel
tunnel.description: A cramped, dripping tunnel shored up with rotting timbers. It slopes gently uphill, and the floor is scuffed by boots that came this way not so long ago.

exits.description: A narrow door in the tunnel wall.
exits.traversal: The tunnel narrows to a stooping crawl before the narrow door; it squeals on its hinges and opens behind the casks of a cellar.

exits.description: The tunnel climbs toward old stonework.
exits.traversal: The tunnel climbs, slick underfoot, until rough rock gives way to old fitted stonework.

east_road.name: East Road
east_road.lore: Open farmland beyond the village. Travellers, drovers and the odd highwayman use the road.

road.name: East Road
road.description: A rutted dirt road leaving the village between hedgerows and fields. A weathered milestone marks the edge of Riverton; beneath it, carved letters read "Larkspur, two hours" with an arrow pointing east.

exits.description: Back into the village square.
The road runs on east between hedged farmland, over a low rise and out of sight. Larkspur is about two hours' walk.
